newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends lower after range-bound trading.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends lower after range-bound trading.

text.p: The won finished lower versus the dollar on Thursday after being caught in a narrow band throughout the day, traders said.
The won closed at an intraday low of 878.20 after opening at 877.50. It peaked at 877.30.

The recent bullishness of the dollar kept the U.S. unit rising despite an inflow of foreign funds for investment in local stocks and bonds and present fears of a central bank intervention, dealers said.
They said the central bank was rumoured to have offered to sell dollars at 891.50 won in three-month forward trading and at 906.00 won in six-month forward trading in late morning.
But the talk failed to buoy the won.

Expected import deals on Friday and early next week are likely to push the won lower in the near term, traders said. But sharpness of the fall would depend on the central bank's intentions, they added.
"Buy at 877 won and sell at 879," advised one local trader.
The base mid-rate is seen at 877.80 for Friday, unchanged from Thursday. -- JEAN YOON (822) 727 5643
